---
title: "Server Manual"
subtitle: "SimilaritySearchServer: the REST API, the job queue and the two command lines"
lang: en-US
---

`SimilaritySearchServer` provides access to [`SimilaritySearchEngine`](../index.qmd), the
embedded engine documented in the rest of this site, through a REST API, two command lines and
an asynchronous job queue. It implements no indexing logic. **Storage, indexing and search are
implemented in the engine.** This package translates HTTP requests and command lines into
engine calls, and engine results and failures into responses and exit codes.

This division determines where each subject is documented. Questions about projects,
persistence, text profiles or the behavior of a search are answered in the engine's
[architecture guide](../architecture.qmd). The two packages are documented on one site because
the interface between them is the public API of the engine, and both sides of that interface
are described here.

## 1. What this package contains

| file | what it does |
| :--- | :--- |
| `config.jl`, `cli.jl`, `ctl.jl` | TOML configuration, and the two `ArgParse` command lines (`similarity-search`, `similarity-search-admin`) |
| `cli_handlers.jl`, `ctl_handlers.jl` | one function per subcommand: `build`, `search`, `searchbatch`, `allknn`, `fft`, `neardup`, `hsp`, `closestpair`, `describe`, `rebuild`, `dump`, `load`, the follower commands and `postings` |
| `server.jl` | the HTTP API (Oxygen), one `EmbeddedEngine` per dataset, and the request/response mapping |
| `followers_api.jl` | the routes of followers, and the task of `serve` that processes the periodic followers |
| `plugins.jl` | loading the plugins of `[plugins]`, and the wire names of their key sources and kinds of follower |
| `jobs.jl`, `executors.jl` | the job spool: an atomic directory tree (`queued/`, `running/`, `completed/`, `failed/`) of `.job.toml` files, dispatched as independent Julia subprocesses |
| `tokens.jl`, `telemetry.jl` | access tokens, and the `op_log` operation history |
| `compression.jl` | the compression of responses with gzip, and the result of a job sent in parts |
| `interactive.jl` | guided invocation through `REPL.TerminalMenus` |
| `apps/` | the three installable app entry points |

Three clients of the HTTP API are in this directory and are separate packages: `python/`, for
Python, `julia/`, the [Julia client](julia-client.qmd), whose functions have the names of the
engine's functions, and `node/`, the [Node.js client](node-client.qmd), with one method per route.

The schema, the persistence layer, the index engine and project management are not part of this
package. They are `SimilaritySearchEngine.Schema`, `.Persistence`, `.IndexEngine` and
`.Project`.

## 2. How a dataset is held

The server holds one `SimilaritySearchEngine.EmbeddedEngine` per dataset identifier, in
`AppState.handles`. That handle contains the two parts of a project, its RocksDB metadata store
and its search engine, which keeps them consistent across a restart. `reload_datasets!` opens
every dataset under `<workdir>/datasets/` with `open_project`, and a reopened dataset preserves
its index, its text profile, its staged items and its deletion marks.

There is no snapshot file. Earlier versions of this package wrote one JLD2 snapshot per dataset
and read it on demand, because the engine did not store its own index. The engine stores it
now, and a dataset is the directory that contains it.

**A job that operates on an entire dataset runs as a subprocess and opens its project in
read-only mode**, because the serving process may hold the project open, and the RocksDB write
lock is exclusive per process.

## 3. Kinds of project

The parameter `index_kind` of the API names a pair: the type of data a project holds, and the structure that indexes it:

| `index_kind` | engine spec | notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `searchgraph` | `DenseVectors(distance; index=Graph())` | approximate, adjusts its own parameters; the default |
| `exhaustive_search` | `DenseVectors(distance; index=Exhaustive())` | exact, linear scan |
| `parallel_exhaustive_search` | `DenseVectors(distance; index=Exhaustive(parallel=true))` | exact, data-parallel |
| `bm25_invfile` | `TextDocuments(FitFromCorpus(); index=BM25())` | BM25 scoring |
| `invfile` | `TextDocuments(FitFromCorpus(); index=VectorSpace(distance))` | TF-IDF cosine |
| `sparse_invfile` | `SparseVectors(dimension, distance)` | sparse vectors encoded by the caller; requires `dimension` |

The server builds the spec from the fields of the request with `dataset_spec(index_kind, distance, dimension, storage)`. When the request gives no distance, a dense dataset uses `SqL2`, and `invfile` and `sparse_invfile` use `NormCosine`. BM25 scoring does not use a distance. See [Project Specifications](../architecture.qmd#project-specifications) in the engine manual.

The names of `distance` are `L2`, `SqL2`, `Cosine`, `NormCosine`, `Angle` and `NormAngle`, in
upper or lower case. `L2` is computed as `SqL2`, which orders the results in the same way.
Another name is refused with `400` and the kind `InvalidOption`. Until 2026-11-23 the server
also listed `jaccard`, and a dataset created with it failed with `500`. `storage` selects how a
dense dataset stores its vectors (see "Storage of Dense Vectors").

A text project is created with `FitFromCorpus`. Its vocabulary is fitted from the documents the
dataset has received when `index!` is called for the first time. Sending a pre-computed text
profile to the server is not available over HTTP.

## 4. REST API (base endpoints)

Every response of this API is JSON. A response that succeeded carries `status`; one that
failed carries `error` and `kind` (section 5). The bodies below are real responses, not
sketches.

Two names identify an item, everywhere and with one meaning each: **`doc_id`** is the
identifier the caller gave it, which may be absent, and **`_id`** is the integer the engine
assigned, which is always there. A search result, a stored record and the operation log all
use them that way. Until 2026-09-14 a search result called the first `id` and the second
`doc_id`, so `result.doc_id` and `record.doc_id` were different things; that is corrected,
with no alias for the old names.

At the top level of a response, `id` is the dataset: `{"status":"appended","id":"ds"}`.

### Control

- `GET /healthz` — the process answers HTTP.
- `GET /readyz` — the process is ready to serve. `{"status":"ok"}`.
- `GET /metrics` — metrics in Prometheus text format: documents and deleted records per
  dataset, jobs in progress, searches running and waiting, and the counters the operation log
  feeds — requests per dataset and operation, distance computations, items inserted, and a
  histogram of request durations.

The counters cover the running process and start at zero when it starts, which is what a
Prometheus counter is expected to do; `simsearch_process_start_time_seconds` reports when
that was. They are accumulated as each request is recorded, not read back from the operation
log: a collector polls every few seconds, and reading a column family that grows with every
request would cost more than the requests it measures. The log remains the durable record and
is read through `GET /api/v1/datasets/{id}/log`.

### Datasets

- `POST /api/v1/datasets` — creates one. Accepts `id`, `index_kind` (see section 3),
  `distance`, `dimension`, an optional `meta_schema`, `edit_correction` for a text dataset,
  `partition_by` for a text or dense dataset, `partition_graph_min` for a dense dataset
  with `partition_by`, `storage` for a dense dataset, and `max_k`, the largest `k` of a search
  (see "Size of a Response"). Answers `201`. The fields `join_group`,
  `holds_metadata` and `key` were removed on 2026-11-10, and a request that contains one of
  them answers `400` (see "Searching Several Text Fields").
- `GET /api/v1/datasets?offset=&limit=` — every dataset on disk, loaded or not.
- `GET /api/v1/datasets/{id}` — one of them. A dataset with followers also has `followers`,
  the status of each one (see "Followers").
- `DELETE /api/v1/datasets/{id}` — destroys it. A dataset with followers answers `409` with
  the kind `HasFollowers`: its followers are deleted first.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/datasets/{id}/unload` and `/reload` — closes or reopens a dataset
  without restarting the server. The `rebuild` subcommand of the command line requires this,
  because the RocksDB write lock is exclusive per process. `/reload` accepts an optional body
  `{"edit_correction": true}` or `false`, which changes that setting and reopens the dataset
  with it, and `{"max_k": n}`, which changes `max_k`.

```json
POST /api/v1/datasets          {"status":"created","id":"ds"}
DELETE /api/v1/datasets/{id}   {"status":"deleted","id":"ds"}
POST .../unload                {"status":"unloaded","id":"ds"}
POST .../reload                {"status":"reloaded","id":"ds"}

GET /api/v1/datasets/{id}
{"id":"ds", "index_kind":"searchgraph", "distance":"L2",
 "created_at":"2026-09-14T19:41:57.059", "loaded":true,
 "doc_count":5, "tombstone_count":0, "tombstone_ratio":0,
 "edit_correction":false, "max_k":100,
 "meta_schema":[{"name":"year","type":"int64"}], "partition_by":null,
 "beamsearch_baseline":{"bsize":4,"delta":1,"maxvisits":1000000},
 "storage":{"kind":"float32"}, "encoder":null}
```

`GET /api/v1/datasets` wraps a list of those objects: `{"status":"ok", "datasets":[...],
"total":2, "offset":0, "limit":2}`. `doc_count`, `tombstone_count`, `tombstone_ratio`,
`meta_schema`, `partition_by`, `partition_graph_min`, `beamsearch_baseline`, `storage` and
`encoder` are reported for a dataset that is open;
`beamsearch_baseline` is `null` for one that is not backed by a graph, `meta_schema` is
`null` for one that declares nothing, and `storage` and `encoder` are `null` for one that is
not dense. `encoder` is `null` for a dense dataset of `Float32` vectors.

`meta_schema` declares which fields of an item's metadata the dataset expects and what each
one holds:

```json
{"id": "papers", "index_kind": "bm25_invfile",
 "meta_schema": [{"name": "year", "type": "int64"},
                 {"name": "published", "type": "timestamp"}]}
```

The types are `string`, `int64`, `float64`, `bool` and `timestamp`. An append is refused with
`400` when a declared field carries another type. Declaring is additive: a field that is not
declared is stored as it arrives, and a dataset that declares nothing behaves as before. The
declared fields are not indexed; what the declaration changes is that a filter compares in
the declared type, so a `timestamp` is compared as an instant rather than as the text that
stores it. The engine holds the declaration inside the project, which is why it survives a
restart and travels with `dump`.

`edit_correction` applies to a text dataset (`bm25_invfile` or `invfile`). When it is `true`,
`ftsearch` corrects a query token that is absent from the vocabulary to the only vocabulary
token at Damerau-Levenshtein distance 1 from it. For example, `Frankenstien` is searched as
`Frankenstein`. The Damerau-Levenshtein distance counts insertions, deletions, substitutions
and exchanges of two adjacent letters. If two or more vocabulary tokens are at distance 1, the
query token is not replaced.

The default is `false` because the correction has a cost. The server builds an edit index from
the vocabulary each time it opens the dataset: at startup, and at each `/reload`. Measured on
2026-09-24 over a vocabulary of 730,320 tokens, building it took 1.2 s with 64 threads and 5.0
s with one thread, and it used 81 MiB. A query with one token absent from the vocabulary took
18.7 ms to resolve instead of 7.3 µs. A query whose tokens are all in the vocabulary is not
slower.

The value is stored in `descriptor.json`, next to the project, and it travels with `dump` and
`load`. `true` for a dataset that does not hold text is refused with `400`, at creation and at
`/reload`; a refused `/reload` leaves the dataset loaded as it was.

The command line has the same option for a batch of queries:
`similarity-search searchbatch --edit-correction`. It does not read `descriptor.json`: the
flag decides it for that run. On a dataset without text the command exits with code 2.

`partition_by` names a metadata field of a text dataset as its partition field. Each value of
that field is a partition. A text search can then name one partition, and it evaluates only
the items of that partition. Each result has the score that the search over the whole dataset
gives it. The value of the field in an item is a non-empty string or a list of them. An item
whose value is anything else is refused with `400` and the kind `PayloadMismatch`, and no item
of that request is stored. The engine stores the field inside the project, so it is not in
`descriptor.json`, and `dump`, `load` and `rebuild` keep it. `partition_by` on a sparse
dataset is refused with `400`.

On a dense dataset, a search can name one partition too (since 2026-11-18). A partition shares
the vectors of the dataset and copies none.

- A partition with fewer than `partition_graph_min` indexed members is searched with an exact
  scan of its members. The default is 4,096.
- A larger partition of a `searchgraph` dataset has its own graph, which each append builds or
  extends. Its results are approximate, as those of the dataset's own graph.
- Every partition of an exact dataset (`exhaustive_search`, `parallel_exhaustive_search`) is
  scanned.

`partition_graph_min` is stored inside the project. It is refused with `400` on a dataset that
is not dense, without `partition_by`, or when it is not an integer.

- `GET /api/v1/datasets/{id}/partitions` — the partition field and the partitions, sorted by
  name, each with the number of items appended to it and `graph`, whether it has its own
  graph. Deleted items and items not indexed yet are counted. `graph` is `false` for every
  partition of a text dataset, and `partition_graph_min` is `null` for one. A dataset without
  a partition field answers `400`.

```json
{"status":"ok","id":"ds","partition_by":"repo","partition_graph_min":150,
 "partitions":[{"name":"otro","items":200,"graph":true},
               {"name":"tres","items":100,"graph":false}]}
```

The command line has `similarity-search build --partition-by <field>`,
`similarity-search build --partition-graph-min <n>` for a dense dataset, and
`similarity-search searchbatch --partition <name>`.

A partition follower (see "Followers") divides the items in the same way, outside the project.
A dataset can have several, and `migrate-partitions` moves the partitions of `partition_by` to
one.

### Storage of Dense Vectors

A dense dataset stores each vector in one of three forms. The field `storage` of
`POST /api/v1/datasets` selects the form, and only its `kind` is required. The default is
`float32`. The engine manual describes each form in
[Quantized Dense Indexes](../architecture.qmd#quantized-dense-indexes) and
[Sketched Dense Indexes](../architecture.qmd#sketched-dense-indexes).

| `kind` | engine storage | bytes per vector of dimension `d` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `float32` | `Float32Vectors()` | `4 d` |
| `quantized` | `Quantized(SQ(bits; range); rotation, keep_vectors)` | `d × bits / 8`, and 8 more with the range `per_vector` |
| `sketched` | `Sketched(hyperplanes; bits, rerank, keep_vectors, center, ...)` | `hyperplanes × bits / 8` |

```json
{"id": "papers", "index_kind": "searchgraph", "distance": "NormCosine",
 "storage": {"kind": "quantized", "bits": 4}}
```

The fields of `quantized`:

| field | value | default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `bits` | 8, 4 or 2 bits per coordinate | 8 |
| `range` | `global`, one range for every coordinate of every vector, or `per_vector`, one range for each vector | `global` |
| `minmax` | `[lo, hi]`, the range of `global`, given instead of estimated | `null` |
| `samplesize` | the number of vectors the range is estimated from | 4096 |
| `rotation` | `none`, `qr` or `hadamard` | `none` |
| `keep_vectors` | keep the `Float32` vectors on disk next to the codes | `false` |

The fields of `sketched`:

| field | value | default |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `hyperplanes` | the number of hyperplanes, a multiple of 64 | 256 |
| `bits` | 1, 2, 4 or 8 bits per hyperplane | 8 |
| `rerank` | 0, or the number of candidates, as a multiple of `k`, that are evaluated again with the `Float32` vectors; a value above 0 needs `keep_vectors` | 0 |
| `keep_vectors` | keep the `Float32` vectors on disk next to the sketches | `false` |
| `center` | subtract the mean of the fitting sample from each vector and each query | `false` |
| `samplesize`, `hsel`, `henc`, `entquantile`, `anchorpolicy` | the options of the fitting, described in the engine manual | 16384, 16 × `hyperplanes`, 1024, 0.5, `random` |

A field that is absent takes the default of the engine. `GET /api/v1/datasets/{id}` reports
`storage` with every field, and `encoder`:

```json
{"id":"vecs", "index_kind":"exhaustive_search", "distance":"NormCosine", ...,
 "storage":{"kind":"quantized", "bits":8, "range":"global", "minmax":null,
            "samplesize":4096, "rotation":"none", "keep_vectors":false},
 "encoder":{"fitted":true, "dimension":4, "min":0.0, "max":1.7000009,
            "bytes_per_vector":4, "staged":0}}
```

- `fitted` is whether the encoder exists.
- `dimension` is the dimension of the vectors, or `null` before the encoder exists.
- `min` and `max` are the range of a global quantizer or of sketches of 2 to 8 bits, and
  `null` otherwise.
- `bytes_per_vector` is the size of one code.
- `staged` is the number of appended vectors that are not encoded yet.
- A sketched dataset also reports `bytes_on_disk_per_vector`, which includes the kept vectors.

The storage and the encoder are saved inside the project, not in `descriptor.json`. `dump`,
`load` and `rebuild` keep the storage, and `dump` and `load` also keep the fitted encoder.

**Measurements.** Measured on 2026-11-23 on SISAP 2025 `ccnews` (dev): 603,664 vectors of
dimension 384, the distance `NormCosine`, an `exhaustive_search` dataset, and the first 1,000
`otest` queries. Recall@10 is the fraction of the exact 10 nearest neighbors in the results.
The engine ran with 32 threads on a Xeon Silver 4216. The column `searchbatch` divides the time
of one batch of 1,000 queries by 1,000. The column `search` is the time of one query, which an
exact scan answers with one thread. The disk column is the whole project directory.

| storage | bytes per vector | recall@10 | `searchbatch`, ms | `search`, ms | disk |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `float32` | 1,536 | 0.999 | 5.36 | 110 | 1,593 MB |
| `quantized`, 8 bits | 384 | 0.988 | 1.95 | 36 | 441 MB |
| `quantized`, 4 bits | 192 | 0.909 | 2.06 | 28 | 249 MB |
| `quantized`, 2 bits | 96 | 0.757 | 3.37 | 28 | 153 MB |
| `sketched`, the defaults (256 hyperplanes, 8 bits) | 256 | 0.490 | 0.92 | 19 | 313 MB |
| `sketched`, the defaults, `rerank` 4, `keep_vectors` | 256 | 0.734 | 0.86 | 23 | 1,849 MB |

Encoding the 603,664 vectors took 2 to 3 s for a quantized dataset and 2 to 7 s for a sketched
one.

**Which storage to use.** For the vectors of a language model, use `quantized`. On `ccnews`, 8
bits kept a recall@10 of 0.988 with a quarter of the bytes, and 4 bits kept 0.909 with an
eighth. At the same memory, sketches gave a lower recall: 0.49 with 256 bytes per vector. A
sketch is defined by distances only, so `sketched` takes the distances that `quantized` does
not: `Angle` and `NormAngle`. `quantized` takes `L2`, `SqL2`, `Cosine` and `NormCosine`. A
second evaluation (`rerank`) raises the recall of sketches, but it needs the `Float32` vectors
on disk.

**Rotation and centering.** Both are off by default. Whether to use them is a decision of the
user, and the facts are these:

- `rotation` applies to `quantized`. A random rotation gives every coordinate the same scale
  before the quantization. The coordinates of the vectors of most neural embedding models
  already have similar scales: on `ccnews`, a QR rotation changed recall@10 by less than 0.01
  at every width. Use `qr` for vectors that are not normalized, for vectors of several models in
  one dataset, for features that a neural model did not produce, or when the recall on a sample
  of queries is clearly below that of an exact search. `qr` costs `d²` operations for each query
  and each inserted vector, and `4 d²` bytes of storage: 4 MB at dimension 1024. `hadamard`
  costs `d log d` operations, and the dimension must be a power of two.
- `center` applies to `sketched`. It subtracts the mean of the fitting sample from every vector
  and every query. Under `L2` and `SqL2` it changes no distance, because those distances do not
  change when every vector moves by the same amount. Under `Cosine` and `NormCosine` it changes
  the angles between the vectors. The vectors of a language model seldom need it. A rotation
  changes no distance, so `sketched` has no rotation.

**Fitting.** An append indexes its items, so the first append fits the encoder on its own
vectors, on at most `samplesize` of them. A quantized dataset whose first request has a few
vectors estimates its range from those few. Send at least `samplesize` vectors in the first
request, 4096 with the defaults, or give `minmax`. A sketched dataset fits its encoder on more
than 64 vectors. Before that, its vectors stay staged, `encoder.staged` counts them, and a
search answers `409`:

```json
{"kind":"NotTrained","error":"this sketched project holds 1 staged vector(s) and no encoder: the encoder is fitted at an index! with more than 64 staged vectors, and until then the project has nothing to search"}
```

**Distances of the results.** A quantized dataset reports the distance between the query, in
`Float32`, and the codes, which is close to the distance of the dataset. A sketched dataset
without `rerank` reports the distance between sketches: the number of different bits at 1 bit,
and the squared Euclidean distance between the codes at 2, 4 and 8 bits. That distance orders
the results, and it is not the distance of the dataset. With `rerank` above 0, the results
have the distance of the dataset.

**The `Float32` vectors.** With `keep_vectors` set to `false`, the default, the `Float32`
vectors are removed once they are encoded. `fetch` does not return the vector of an item with
any storage. `rebuild` encodes the kept vectors again with a new encoder. It refuses a quantized
or sketched dataset without them, exits with code 2, and leaves the dataset as it was.

**Errors.** A `storage` is refused with `400` and the kind `InvalidOption` when its kind or one
of its fields is unknown, when a value has the wrong type or is out of range, when the dataset
is not dense, or when the storage does not take the distance:

```json
{"kind":"InvalidOption","error":"the storage quantized has no field(s) bitz; it takes bits, range, minmax, samplesize, rotation, keep_vectors"}
{"kind":"InvalidOption","error":"a quantized project searches with SqL2, L2, L1, Cosine or NormCosine; Angle has no distance over codes"}
```

The command line takes the same object: `similarity-search build --storage '{"kind":
"quantized", "bits": 4}'`. `describe` reports the distance of the dataset, `storage` and
`encoder`. Its `distance_stats` search with the kept vectors, and they are `null` without them
or for a sketched dataset without `rerank`.

### Search and indexing

- `POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/append` — inserts items. A dense item contains `vector`, a text
  item contains `text`, and a sparse item contains `indices` and `values`. The fields
  `doc_id`, `keywords` and `refs`, and any other field, become the metadata of the item.
- `POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/search` — dense and sparse search, with `vector`, `k`, and
  optional `filter`, `beamsearch_overrides`, and `partition` for a dense dataset with a partition
  field. `k` is 10 when it is absent, and at most `max_k` of the dataset (see "Size of a
  Response"). `filter` applies to the results of the partition. A partition name the dataset does
  not hold answers `404` with the kind `UnknownPartition`. `partition` on a dataset without a
  partition field, or together with `beamsearch_overrides`, answers `400`: the overrides
  apply to the graph of the whole dataset.
- `POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/ftsearch` — text search. Accepts `text`, `k`, an optional
  `filter` in the format of `search`, and `partition` for a dataset with a partition field.
  `text` must be a string. A filtered text search reads the same bounded number of candidates
  as a filtered `search`. A partition name the dataset does not hold answers
  `404` with the kind `UnknownPartition`, and the message lists the closest names. `partition`
  on a dataset without a partition field answers `400`.
- `POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/fetch` and `GET /api/v1/datasets/{id}/exists?ids=` — records by
  identifier, and whether an identifier exists.
- `POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/delete` — logical deletion. Takes `_id`, the integer a search
  or a fetch reported.
- `POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/calibrate` — recall calibration for a graph-backed project.
  Accepts `minrecall`, `numqueries`, `ksearch`, `queries`, and the shape of the tuning goal,
  `tradeoff` and `transition` (see the `calibrate!` section of the getting-started tutorial).
  The response reports the configuration as `baseline` and the recall it reaches as
  `calibration`, measured on queries that took no part in the tuning, with a 95% interval.
  `partition` calibrates the graph of one partition of a dense dataset instead. Its levels are
  stored apart, the response carries `partition`, and `beamsearch_baseline` of the dataset
  does not change. A partition without its own graph answers `400` with the kind
  `InvalidOption`, because an exact scan has nothing to calibrate.
- `POST /api/v1/search/hybrid` — reciprocal rank fusion over two datasets.

```json
POST .../append     {"status":"appended","id":"ds","inserted":5}
POST .../delete     {"status":"soft_deleted","id":"ds","_id":1}
POST .../calibrate  {"status":"calibrated","id":"ds",
                     "baseline":{"bsize":12,"delta":1.05,"maxvisits":934},
                     "calibration":{"minrecall":0.9,"recall":0.9323,"recall_lo":0.9062,
                                    "recall_hi":0.9549,"confidence":0.95,"numqueries":64,
                                    "distance_evaluations":317.2,"heldout":true}}

POST .../search  and  POST .../ftsearch
{"status":"searched","id":"ds",
 "results":[{"doc_id":"d1","_id":1,"distance":0},
            {"doc_id":"d2","_id":2,"distance":1}]}

POST .../fetch
{"status":"fetched","id":"ds",
 "results":[{"doc_id":"d1","_id":1,"keywords":["k1"],"refs":[],
             "schema_version":1,"year":2021}]}

GET .../exists?ids=d1,nope
{"status":"ok","id":"ds",
 "results":[{"id":"d1","doc_id":"d1","_id":1,"exists":true,"deleted":false},
            {"id":"nope","doc_id":null,"_id":null,"exists":false,"deleted":false}]}

POST /api/v1/search/hybrid
{"status":"searched","results":[{"doc_id":"d1","_id":1,"score":0.0327}]}
```

A `fetch` result merges the item's metadata into the record, which is why `year` sits beside
`keywords` above. In `exists`, `id` is the string that was asked about, which may be either
identifier; `doc_id` and `_id` are what it resolved to, and are `null` when nothing did. A `search` over a text dataset reports a BM25 score with its sign inverted,
under the name `distance`, which is the convention of the library: a smaller value is a closer
match. A filtered search that could not fill `k` adds `"insufficient_results":true`, since it
reads a bounded number of candidates before applying the filter.

An operation on one dataset is addressed under that dataset. The two queries that read more
than one are under `/api/v1/search/`, which is the only place where a route is not about a
single dataset. The earlier prefix `/api/v1/simsearch/` was removed on 2026-09-13: it marked a
distinction that the API stopped making.

### Size of a Response

A search answers its `k` results in one response. The server has no cursors and no
`page_size` since 2026-11-23. The server computed every result before it sent the first page,
so a cursor divided the response and saved no computation. A request with `page_size` answers
`400` with the kind `InvalidOption`.

**`max_k`** is the largest `k` that a search of a dataset can ask for. It is 100 when the
dataset is created without it. It is a setting of the dataset, kept in `descriptor.json`:

- `POST /api/v1/datasets` with `"max_k": 1000` sets it when the dataset is created.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/datasets/{id}/reload` with the body `{"max_k": 1000}` changes it.
- `similarity-search build --max-k 1000` sets it for a dataset of the command line. `dump` and
  `load` keep it.
- `GET /api/v1/datasets/{id}` and `describe` report it. A dataset created before 2026-11-23
  has 100.

A search with a larger `k` answers `400` with the kind `InvalidOption`, and the message says
how to change `max_k`:

```json
POST .../search  {"vector": [...], "k": 500}   [400]
{"kind":"InvalidOption",
 "error":"k = 500 is larger than max_k = 100 of the dataset 'ds'. max_k is set when ..."}
```

`max_k` limits `search`, `ftsearch`, the searches of a follower, which use `max_k` of the
leader, and the hybrid search, whose `k` is at most `max_k` of each of its two datasets. It
does not limit the jobs, whose results go to a file, or the commands of `similarity-search`.
It does not limit `fetch` or a posting list either, and a posting list takes `limit`.

**Compression.** The server compresses a response with gzip when the request accepts it
(`Accept-Encoding: gzip`) and the body has at least `[server] gzip_min_bytes` bytes, 1024 by
default. The response then has `Content-Encoding: gzip`. The Julia, the Python and the Node.js
clients accept gzip and decompress it, so a caller of a client does nothing. On 2026-11-23, the 200
results of a search over 200 paragraphs of *Frankenstein* took 11,984 bytes, and 2,161 bytes
compressed. `[server] gzip = false` turns the compression off (section 6).

`GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/result` sends the file of the result in parts, without reading it
into memory, and compresses it as it is read when the request accepts gzip.

### Followers

A **follower** is a dataset that organizes the items of another dataset, its **leader**. It
reads the items of the leader and does not copy them. It is stored in
`<workdir>/datasets/<leader>.followers/<name>/`, outside the directory of the leader, and it is
created and deleted without a change to the items of the leader. There are two kinds:

- A **partition follower** divides the items of a text or a dense dataset into partitions, one
  per key. A search in one partition evaluates only the items of that partition. Each result
  has the score or the distance that the search over the whole dataset gives it.
- A **keyword follower** indexes the keys of each item in an inverted file. It searches the
  items by a set of keys, and it returns the posting list of one key: the `_id`s of the items
  that hold it. The leader can be a dataset of any kind.

The **source** of a follower says where the keys of an item come from: `keywords`, `refs`,
`doc_id`, or `meta:<field>`, a field of the metadata of the item. A key is a non-empty string.
A follower cannot process an item whose source holds another value, such as a number. When the
follower is created, the request answers `400` with the kind `PayloadMismatch`, and the
follower is not created. When such an item arrives after the follower exists, the leader
stores it, and the follower stays at the item before it. The `append` answers `200`, and the
status of the follower has the error. `POST .../followers/{name}/sync` answers the error. The
[architecture page](../architecture.qmd#leader-and-follower-datasets) describes how the engine
stores and processes followers.

`POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/followers` creates a follower and processes every indexed item of
the leader before it answers:

```json
{"name": "by_section", "kind": "partition", "source": "meta:section",
 "disjoint": true, "policy": "on_index"}
```

| field | values |
| :--- | :--- |
| `name` | letters, digits, `_` and `-`, at most 128 characters |
| `kind` | `partition` or `keyword` |
| `source` | `keywords`, `refs`, `doc_id`, or `meta:<field>` |
| `disjoint` | a partition follower only. `true` (the default): an item has at most one key, and an item with several keys raises `PayloadMismatch`, as a value that is not a string does. `false`: an item belongs to the partition of each of its keys |
| `graph_min` | a partition follower of a dense dataset only: the number of members from which a partition has its own graph, as `partition_graph_min` |
| `distance` | a keyword follower only: `jaccard` (the default), `dice`, `intersection` or `cosine_set` |
| `policy` | `on_index` (the default), `on_write`, `manual`, or `{"periodic": {"seconds": 60, "items": 1000}}` |

A field or a value that the server does not know answers `400`. A follower accepts no direct
write: `append` and `delete` go to the leader. A deleted item stays in the structures of a
follower, and the server removes it from each result, as it does for the leader.

The **position** of a follower is the last `_id` of the leader that it processed, and its
**lag** is the number of indexed items of the leader after that position. A follower that lags
answers with the items it has processed. The policy says when it processes the new items:

| policy | when |
| :--- | :--- |
| `on_index` | inside each `append`, after the leader indexes the new items. The response of `append` comes after the follower is processed |
| `on_write` | another name of `on_index` since 2026-11-23 |
| `manual` | only at `POST .../followers/{name}/sync` |
| `periodic` | inside an `append` that leaves the follower `items` or more items behind its leader. In a task of `serve`, when `seconds` have passed since its last processing, or when its lag reaches `items`. The task checks every `[followers] check_seconds` seconds (section 6) |

Before 2026-11-23, `on_write` processed the new items after the leader stored them and before
it indexed them. A follower processes indexed items only, so a follower of a `searchgraph` or a
text dataset processed them at the next `append`. A follower created with `on_write` keeps the
name, and it processes the items as `on_index`.

A follower that fails during an `append` does not undo the write of the leader, and it does not
change the response of the `append`. The `append` answers `200` with the number of items it
stored. The follower stays at the item it could not process, the server writes the error to its
log, and the status of the follower has `error`. Before 2026-11-23, the `append` answered the
error of the follower, and a client that sent the request again stored the items twice.

The routes of a follower are under its leader. `{f}` is the name of a follower, or
`name=value` for one partition, with a character that a path segment does not allow encoded
with `%`. The permission is the one of the leader:

| route | permission | what it does |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `POST /datasets/{id}/followers` | admin | creates a follower; `201` with its status |
| `GET /datasets/{id}/followers` | read | the status of every follower |
| `GET /datasets/{id}/followers/{f}` | read | the status of one follower |
| `DELETE /datasets/{id}/followers/{f}` | admin | deletes a follower |
| `POST /datasets/{id}/followers/{f}/sync` | write | processes the new items now |
| `POST /datasets/{id}/followers/{f}/rebuild` | admin | builds the follower again from every indexed item |
| `GET /datasets/{id}/followers/{f}/partitions` | read | the partitions of a partition follower |
| `POST /datasets/{id}/followers/{f}=value/search` | read | `search` in one partition of a dense dataset: `vector`, `k`, `filter`, `minrecall` |
| `POST /datasets/{id}/followers/{f}=value/ftsearch` | read | `ftsearch` in one partition of a text dataset: `text`, `k`, `filter` |
| `POST /datasets/{id}/followers/{f}=value/calibrate` | write | calibrates the graph of one partition: `minrecall`, `numqueries`, `ksearch` |
| `POST /datasets/{id}/followers/{f}/search` | read | a keyword follower: `keys`, `k`, `t`, `filter` |
| `GET /datasets/{id}/followers/{f}/postings?key=&limit=` | read | the posting list of one key of a keyword follower |
| `GET /datasets/{id}/postings?key=&limit=` | read | the posting list of a token of a text dataset, or of a dimension of a sparse dataset |
| `POST /datasets/{id}/migrate-partitions` | admin | moves the partitions of `partition_by` to a partition follower: `name`, `disjoint` |
| `GET /datasets/{id}/group` | read | the leader and the status of every follower |

All routes are under `/api/v1`. The searches answer in the shape of the searches of a dataset.
`t` is the number of keys of the query that an item must hold to be a candidate; the default is
`1`. A posting list holds the `_id`s in ascending order, and `limit=n` returns the first `n`.
A posting list of a frequent key in a large dataset can hold most of the items of the dataset,
and it is sent in one response. There is no route that lists the keys of a keyword follower.

```json
POST /api/v1/datasets/demo/followers  [201]
{"status":"created","name":"demo/kw","leader":"demo","kind":"KeywordFollower",
 "source":"Keywords()","policy":"OnIndex()","plugin":null,"position":3,
 "leader_indexed":3,"lag":0,"synchronized":true,"stale":false,"missing":false,"open":true,
 "stats":{"keys":2,"postings":4,"items_without_keys":0,"shortest":2,"median":2,"longest":2}}

POST .../followers/by_section=calle/ftsearch   {"text": "gato", "k": 5}
{"status":"searched","id":"demo","insufficient_results":true,
 "results":[{"doc_id":"d3","_id":3,"distance":-0.8908208}]}

POST .../followers/kw/search   {"keys": ["gato", "perro"], "k": 5}
{"status":"searched","id":"demo","insufficient_results":true,
 "results":[{"doc_id":"d3","_id":3,"distance":0.0},{"doc_id":"d1","_id":1,"distance":0.5},
            {"doc_id":"d2","_id":2,"distance":0.5}]}

GET .../followers/kw/postings?key=gato   {"id":"demo","follower":"kw","key":"gato","ids":[1,3]}
GET .../postings?key=calle&limit=10      {"id":"demo","key":"calle","ids":[2,3]}

GET .../followers/by_section/partitions
{"id":"demo","follower":"by_section",
 "partitions":[{"name":"calle","items":2,"graph":false},{"name":"casa","items":1,"graph":false}]}

POST .../followers/m/sync
{"status":"synchronized","processed":1,"name":"demo/m","position":4,"lag":0, ...}
```

A status has the fields of the engine's `FollowerStatus`. `kind`, `source` and `policy` are
the text of the engine, such as `PartitionFollower`, `MetaValue("section")` and
`Periodic(seconds=60.0, items=nothing)`. `stale` is `true` when the leader was rebuilt after
the follower processed its items. `missing` is `true` when the leader lists the follower and its
directory does not exist. `stats` holds the statistics of the kind: for a partition follower,
`partitions`, `memberships`, `smallest`, `median`, `largest` and `graphs`. A follower whose
last processing failed, or that `serve` could not open, has `error`, the message of its last
failure.
`GET /api/v1/datasets/{id}` has `followers`, the status of each follower.

`serve` opens the followers of each dataset when it loads or reloads the dataset. A follower
that cannot be opened stays closed, its status has `error`, and the leader stays available.
`DELETE /api/v1/datasets/{id}` of a leader with followers answers `409` with the kind
`HasFollowers`, and the message names each follower. Each one is deleted first.

The errors of a follower have kinds of their own:

| kind | status | when |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| `UnknownFollower` | 404 | the leader has no follower with that name |
| `UnknownPartition` | 404 | the partition follower has no partition with that value; the message lists the closest names |
| `PluginNotLoaded` | 404 | the follower needs a plugin that this server has not loaded |
| `StaleFollower` | 409 | the leader was rebuilt after the follower processed its items; `rebuild` of the follower builds it again |
| `HasFollowers` | 409 | a leader with followers cannot be deleted |

A partition follower is an alternative to `partition_by`. The partitions of `partition_by` are
in the project of the dataset, and an item has one partition per value. A partition follower is
outside the project, a dataset can have several, and a non-disjoint one puts an item in each
partition it names. `POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/migrate-partitions` moves the partitions of
`partition_by` to a partition follower over `meta:<field>`, with the same `partition_graph_min`.
`disjoint` has no default. After the migration the dataset has no partition field, and a search
with `partition` answers `400` with a message that names the followers.

The command line `similarity-search` has the same operations on a working directory:

```bash
similarity-search follower-create --dataset demo --name kw --kind keyword --source keywords
similarity-search follower-create --dataset demo --name by_section --kind partition \
      --source meta:section [--non-disjoint] [--graph-min N] [--policy manual]
similarity-search follower-list --dataset demo
similarity-search follower-sync --dataset demo --name kw
similarity-search follower-rebuild --dataset demo --name kw
similarity-search follower-delete --dataset demo --name kw
similarity-search migrate-partitions --dataset vec --name group --disjoint true
similarity-search postings --dataset demo --follower kw --key gato [--limit N]
similarity-search searchbatch --dataset demo --queries q.jsonl --output out.jsonl --follower by_section=calle
```

`searchbatch --follower name=value` searches one partition. `searchbatch --follower name` of a
keyword follower reads `keys`, and optionally `t`, from each query line. `describe` lists the
followers. `follower-list`, `postings`, `describe` and `searchbatch` open the dataset read-only,
so they run while a server holds it. The other commands write the dataset: when another process
holds it, such as a running server, they exit with code 5 and say to use
`similarity-search-ctl`. `similarity-search-ctl` has `followers` (the group view),
`follower-create`, `follower-sync`, `follower-rebuild`, `follower-delete` and
`migrate-partitions`, with the same arguments, and calls the routes above.

`rebuild` creates a new project, so the `_id`s of the items can change. It attaches the
followers to the new project and prints the state of each one. A follower of the new project is
stale until it is rebuilt, and `--rebuild-followers` rebuilds every one in the same command:

```text
Rebuild completed for 'demo': 4 item(s) reindexed into ./workdir/datasets/demo
  follower demo/by_section: stale; build it again with similarity-search follower-rebuild --dataset demo --name by_section
  follower demo/kw: stale; build it again with similarity-search follower-rebuild --dataset demo --name kw
```

`dump` copies the followers to `followers/` of the bundle, and `manifest.json` lists them. It
copies them before the project. A server can append items during a `dump`, and this order
ensures that a follower in the bundle has not processed an item that the project in the bundle
does not have. `load` copies the followers next to the new dataset and attaches them to it. The
project and its followers come from the same bundle, so the followers are not stale.

### Plugins

A **plugin** is a Julia module that adds key sources and kinds of follower to the server. It is a
`.jl` file or a package. A plugin that needs a program outside Julia calls it from its own code,
for example with `run`. The code of a plugin runs in the process of the server, with the
permissions of that process, and only the configuration file declares plugins.

A plugin is declared in `config.toml`:

```toml
[plugins.Decades]
path = "plugins/decades.jl"     # a file that defines `module Decades`, relative to this file
# package = "Decades"           # or a package of the active environment: one of the two

[plugins.Decades.settings]      # optional; passed to Decades.setup(settings)
labels = "short"
```

The name of the table is the name of the module, and the name of the plugin. `serve` loads the
plugins when it starts, before it opens any dataset. For each one, it includes the file into
`Main` or loads the package, calls the function `setup` of the module with the settings if the
module has one, registers the module in the engine with `register_plugin!`, and reads the wire
names that the module declares. A plugin is loaded once per process. There is no route that
loads a plugin: a new plugin needs a restart of `serve`.

A plugin that cannot be loaded stops the start, and `serve` prints the reason:

```text
Error: the plugin Decades was not loaded: the file /srv/search/plugins/decades.jl does not exist; `path` is relative to the directory of the configuration file
Correct or remove [plugins.Decades] in config.toml, and start the server again.
```

The module does not depend on the server. It declares its wire names with two constants, read
by their names:

```julia
module Decades

using SimilaritySearchEngine
const SSE = SimilaritySearchEngine

"The decade of an integer field of `meta`: 1987 is 1980s."
struct Decade <: SSE.KeySource
    field::String
end

function SSE.keys_of(s::Decade, item::SSE.StoredItem)
    year = get(item.meta, s.field, nothing)
    year isa Integer ? string(10 * fld(year, 10), "s") : nothing
end

# Optional: the settings of [plugins.Decades.settings].
setup(settings::Dict{String,Any}) = nothing

# The wire names. Each constructor takes the options of the request.
const KEY_SOURCES = Dict{String,Function}("decade" => opts -> Decade(opts["field"]))
const FOLLOWER_KINDS = Dict{String,Function}()   # name => (source, opts) -> FollowerSpec

end
```

A key source is a subtype of `KeySource` with a method of `keys_of`, which returns `nothing`, a
string or a list of strings for one item. A kind of follower is a subtype of `FollowerSpec` that
implements the functions of the engine listed in the docstring of `FollowerSpec`. The
[architecture page](../architecture.qmd#leader-and-follower-datasets) describes both. The same
module works in an application that uses the engine alone: it registers the module with
`register_plugin!` and ignores the two constants.

A request names a key source or a kind of a plugin as `Plugin.name`. With options, it is an
object with `name` and the options:

```json
{"name": "by_decade", "kind": "partition",
 "source": {"name": "Decades.decade", "field": "year"}}

{"name": "counts", "kind": {"name": "Counts.key_counts", "min_count": 2},
 "source": "keywords"}
```

A source that starts with `meta:` is the engine's, even when the name of its field has a dot.
A key source of a plugin works with the kinds of the engine, and `disjoint`, `graph_min`,
`distance` and `policy` keep their meaning. A kind of a plugin takes the options in the object
`kind`, and a request that adds `disjoint`, `graph_min` or `distance` to it answers `400`.

| case | status | kind |
| :--- | ---: | :--- |
| the plugin is not loaded | 404 | `PluginNotLoaded`; the message names `[plugins.<Plugin>]` and the loaded plugins |
| the plugin has no such name | 400 | the message lists the names it has |
| the constructor refuses the options | 400 | the message of the constructor; an `EngineError` keeps its kind |

A follower of a kind of a plugin is created, processed, rebuilt, deleted and reported as any
other. Its `plugin` field names the plugin. The search routes and `postings` call the functions
of the engine, which do not know a kind of a plugin, so they answer `400` with the kind
`UnsupportedOperation`. A server that has not loaded the plugin of a follower does not open the
follower: its status has `open` false and the error, a search answers `404` with
`PluginNotLoaded`, and the leader stays available.

- `GET /api/v1/plugins` — the plugins of this process, with the permission `read` over `*`. It
  lists the configuration of the server, not data.

```json
GET /api/v1/plugins
{"status":"ok",
 "plugins":[{"name":"Decades","path":"/srv/search/plugins/decades.jl",
             "key_sources":["Decades.decade"],"follower_kinds":[]}]}
```

`similarity-search` loads the plugins of the file of `--config`, `config.toml` by default, before
the commands that open a follower: `follower-create`, `follower-sync`, `follower-rebuild`,
`rebuild --rebuild-followers`, and `searchbatch` and `postings` with `--follower`. The other
commands do not load them, because loading a plugin compiles its code. A missing file is not an
error; a follower that needs a plugin then fails with exit code 4, and the message names the
file. `follower-create` takes the options of a plugin type as JSON:

```bash
similarity-search --config config.toml follower-create --dataset papers --name by_decade \
      --kind partition --source Decades.decade --source-options '{"field": "year"}'
```

`--kind-options` gives the options of a kind of a plugin in the same way.
`similarity-search-ctl plugins` calls `GET /api/v1/plugins`.

### Searching Several Text Fields

A record can have several text fields, for example a title and an abstract. Each field is a text dataset of its own. Each dataset has its own vocabulary, document frequencies and BM25 length statistics, so a short title is compared with the length of other titles.

- Append each record to every field dataset with the same `doc_id`. Each search result carries that `doc_id`.
- The client keeps the map from field name to dataset id. The server does not keep it.
- The other metadata of the record can be stored in one of the datasets. A `fetch` to that dataset with the `doc_id`s of the results returns it.

The Python client sends one `ftsearch` per field and returns the results by field name:

```python
from similarity_search import SimilaritySearchClient, AsyncSimilaritySearchClient
from similarity_search import ftsearch_fields, ftsearch_fields_async

fields = {"title": "papers_title", "abstract": "papers_abstract"}
client = SimilaritySearchClient("http://127.0.0.1:8080")
hits = ftsearch_fields(client, fields, "redes neuronales", k=5)
# {"title": [{"doc_id": ..., "_id": ..., "distance": ...}, ...], "abstract": [...]}
meta = client.fetch("papers_title", [r["doc_id"] for r in hits["abstract"]])

async with AsyncSimilaritySearchClient("http://127.0.0.1:8080") as aclient:
    hits = await ftsearch_fields_async(aclient, fields, "redes neuronales", k=5)
```

`ftsearch_fields` sends the requests one after the other. `ftsearch_fields_async` sends them at the same time, so it takes the time of the slowest request.

Until 2026-11-10 the server grouped field datasets with the fields `join_group`, `key` and `holds_metadata`, and searched the group with `POST /api/v1/search/group`. That route and `GET /api/v1/datasets/{id}/join_group` were removed. A descriptor written before the removal loses the three fields when it is read, and `load` ignores them in a bundle.

### Vocabulary

- `GET /api/v1/datasets/{id}/vocab?scan=&sample=` — what a text dataset's vocabulary covers.

```json
{"id":"txt", "vocsize":3, "trainsize":3, "numtokens":9, "avgdoclen":3,
 "top_tokens":[{"token":"gato","ndocs":3,"occs":3}],
 "queries":1, "query_tokens":1, "query_oov_tokens":0, "query_oov_rate":0}
```

With `scan=true`, six more fields:

```json
{"live_tokens":9, "live_oov_tokens":0, "live_oov_rate":0,
 "live_documents_scanned":3, "live_documents_total":3, "live_sampled":false}
```

A vocabulary is fitted once and does not grow. The rate over the queries says the words being
asked for are missing, and the rate over the documents says the words the dataset already
holds are missing; the second is what `rebuild` corrects, by refitting the vocabulary over
the documents the dataset has now.

The query counters cost nothing and are always reported. The reading over the documents is
asked for with `scan=true`, and it is bounded: at most `sample` documents are read, spread
evenly over the dataset, and `live_sampled` says whether it read all of them. The default
sample takes about a second whatever the dataset's size; `sample=0` reads every document,
which on a large dataset takes minutes and is better asked for offline with `describe`.
`409` for a dataset that holds no text or was never indexed.

### Telemetry

- `GET /api/v1/datasets/{id}/log?offset=&limit=` — the dataset's `op_log`: one record per
  `search`, `ftsearch`, `append` or `delete`.

```json
{"status":"ok","total":4,"offset":0,"limit":1,
 "entries":[{"operation":"delete","timestamp":"2026-09-14T19:42:11.195",
             "details":{"index_uuid":"ds","_id":1,
                        "user":"alice","token_fingerprint":"703ffec26b6db7b1"}}]}
```

A `search` entry carries more in `details`: `distance_name`, `dimension`,
`distance_evaluations` and `elapsed_seconds`; an `append` entry carries `items_inserted`.

`user` is the name on the token the request carried, and is present when that token was
valid. `token_fingerprint` is the first eight bytes of the token's SHA-256: enough to tell
two tokens of one user apart and to match an entry against a token someone holds, and not
enough to present as one. Until 2026-09-14 this field was the token itself, which put live
credentials in a column family of the dataset and in every `dump` of it. The endpoint still
requires `admin`, because the log says who did what, which is an audit surface rather than a
reading of the dataset.

The number of distance computations of a search is obtained from the engine, in a
`SimilaritySearchEngine.SearchStats` instance that `_run_search` passes to `search` and to
`ftsearch`. It is not obtained by reading a context before and after the call: a search uses a
context taken from a pool of the engine, so a counter read from this package includes the work
of any other search executed since. For `append` the second method is correct, because an
insertion uses the engine's own context under an exclusive write lock.

### Asynchronous jobs

- `POST /api/v1/jobs/{kind}` — enqueues a job (`allknn`, `fft`, `neardup`, `hsp`,
  `searchbatch`, `closestpair`, `build`, `dump`, `load`). Answers `202`.
- `GET /api/v1/jobs?offset=&limit=`, `GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}` and `/result` — the jobs,
  the state of one, and its output.
- `POST /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/block`, `/resume`, `/kill`, and `DELETE /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}`.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/jobs/gc` — removes the finished jobs older than `retention_seconds`.

```json
POST /api/v1/jobs/allknn  [202]   {"status":"accepted","job_id":"fe3198116091f825"}

GET /api/v1/jobs
{"status":"ok","total":1,"offset":0,"limit":1,
 "jobs":[{"id":"fe3198116091f825","kind":"allknn","status":"queued"}]}

POST /api/v1/admin/jobs/gc
{"status":"ok","jobs_purged":[]}
```

A job's state is `queued`, `running`, `blocked`, `completed` or `failed`.
`GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}/result` sends the file the job wrote, in parts, except for `dump`, whose
result is a directory: for that one it answers `{"bundle_dir": ..., "manifest": {...}}`.

A **bundle** of `dump` is a directory with `project/`, a copy of the project, `followers/`,
`manifest.json`, and `dataset.jsonl`. `dataset.jsonl` holds the metadata of each item as one
JSON line, in the order of `_id`:

```json
{"_id":1,"schema_version":1,"doc_id":"d1","keywords":["gato"],"refs":[],"meta":{"year":2001},"deleted":false}
```

A program in any language reads it with a JSON parser. It holds no vectors and no texts.
`load` restores the dataset from `project/`. Then it writes the record and the `meta` of each
line over the copy, so metadata edited in `dataset.jsonl` with a text editor or `jq` takes
effect. `load` reads every line before it copies anything, and a line that is not a JSON
object with `_id` stops it with exit code 2. A bundle without `dataset.jsonl` is loaded from
`project/` alone, and a dataset without items gives an empty `dataset.jsonl`.

Until 2026-11-23 the file was `dataset.avro`, written with Avro. It held the same fields, with
`meta` as a JSON string, and a reader needed a library of Avro. `load` ignores the
`dataset.avro` of an older bundle and writes a warning, because `project/` holds the same
metadata.

The result of `allknn` has one line per item: `{"id", "neighbors", "dists"}`. The result of
`fft` is one object with `centers`, `assign`, `dists`, `covering`, `separation`, `costdists`
and `costblocks`. The result of `neardup` has `centers`, `assign`, `dists`, `duplicate_count`,
`covering`, `epsilon`, `costdists` and `costblocks`. The cost fields of both and the
`covering` and `epsilon` of `neardup` were added on 2026-11-19, so that a client can build the
engine's result types from them.

The record of a failed job (`GET /api/v1/jobs/{job_id}`) has `error` and, since 2026-11-19,
`exit_code`: the exit status of the job's process. The command line exits with a code per
category of engine error (section 5), so `exit_code` tells a client why the job failed. The
message of the engine error is in the output of the process on the server, which the API
does not return.

### Tokens

- `POST /api/v1/admin/tokens` — creates one. Accepts `user`, `permissions` and an optional
  `expires_at`.
- `GET /api/v1/admin/tokens` — every token stored, expired or not.
- `DELETE /api/v1/admin/tokens/{token}` — revokes one.
- `POST /api/v1/admin/tokens/prune` — removes the expired ones.

```json
POST /api/v1/admin/tokens  [201]
{"status":"created","token":"703ffec26b6db7b1...","permissions":["read:*"]}

GET /api/v1/admin/tokens
{"status":"ok",
 "tokens":[{"token":"703ffec26b6db7b1...","user":"alice","permissions":["read:*"],
            "created_at":"2026-09-14T19:42:20.595","expires_at":null}]}

DELETE /api/v1/admin/tokens/{token}   {"status":"revoked"}
POST /api/v1/admin/tokens/prune       {"status":"ok","pruned":0}
```

The token string is returned once, when it is created. `GET /api/v1/admin/tokens` is an audit
listing and reports them in full, which is why it requires `admin`.

### Authentication

Every `/api/v1` endpoint requires a token when `[auth] enabled` is true in `config.toml`.
`/healthz`, `/readyz` and `/metrics` answer without one, so a supervisor and a metrics
collector work without credentials. The default is `false`, which is the behavior of a server
that has never had authentication.

The token travels in the `Authorization` header, as `Bearer <token>` or as the bare token.
A permission is `operation:dataset`:

| operation | grants | includes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `read` | the queries and the `GET` endpoints | — |
| `write` | append, delete, calibrate, job submission | `read` |
| `admin` | dataset creation and deletion, the token endpoints, job control, the operation log | `write` and `read` |

`dataset` is a dataset id or `*`. A route that is not about one dataset — listing datasets,
the job endpoints, the token endpoints — requires the operation over
`*`, so a token restricted to one dataset uses that dataset and cannot enumerate the rest.
`admin:*` grants everything. A request without a valid token is answered `401`; a valid token
without the permission is answered `403`, and the body names the permission that was required.

The first token is created against the working directory, because a server with
authentication enabled refuses to start while no token exists, and the endpoint that creates
tokens is itself behind authentication:

```bash
similarity-search add-token --user admin --permissions "admin:*" --workdir ./workdir
```

Later tokens are created with `POST /api/v1/admin/tokens` or with `similarity-search-ctl
add-token`, which is the same endpoint. A token may carry an `expires_at`, an ISO 8601
timestamp that is verified when the token is created and again on every request.

## 5. How failures are reported

The engine raises typed errors. This package maps them **by category**, never by the text of the message:

| engine category | HTTP | CLI exit code |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| `NotFound` | 404 | 4 |
| `ConflictingState` (staged backlog, untrained profile, empty project) | 409 | 5 |
| `InvalidRequest` (wrong payload, wrong dimension, bad option) | 400 | 2 |
| `StorageFailure` | 500 | 70 |

Two status codes come from this package rather than from the engine: `401` when a request
carries no valid token, and `403` when its token lacks the permission the route requires.

An error response contains two fields: `error`, the message, intended for a person, and `kind`,
the concrete engine type, intended for a client that selects a behavior. Failures detected by a
command line itself, such as a dataset directory that does not exist or an input file that
cannot be read, return exit code `1`. They are detected before the engine is called.

## 6. Configuration

`config.toml` (or `.similarity-search-server.toml`):

```toml
[paths]
workdir = "./workdir"

[server]
host = "127.0.0.1"
port = 8080
gzip = true
gzip_min_bytes = 1024

[resources]
query_threads_pct = 80
batch_threads_pct = 20
max_concurrent_queries = 0

[followers]
check_seconds = 10
```

`gzip` and `gzip_min_bytes` say when a response is compressed (see "Size of a Response"). A
`gzip_min_bytes` that is not a non-negative integer is replaced by the default, 1024.

`check_seconds` is how often the task of `serve` looks for periodic followers to process (see
"Followers"). The section `[plugins]` declares the plugins that `serve` loads when it starts (see
"Plugins"). A follower with `{"periodic": {"seconds": 60}}` is therefore processed between 60
and 70 seconds after its last processing. A value that is not a positive number is replaced by
the default, 10.

`max_concurrent_queries` bounds how many searches run at once. `0` derives it from the split
below: the threads that job execution did not reserve. A request that arrives when every slot
is taken waits for one; it is not refused, because a caller that asked for a search wants the
search. `/metrics` reports `simsearch_queries_running`, `simsearch_queries_waiting`,
`simsearch_query_slots` and `simsearch_query_wait_seconds_total`, which is what says whether
the bound is ever reached.

The bound exists because unbounded concurrency buys no throughput and does cost memory. Past
the number of threads, more concurrent searches share the same cores and each one gets
slower; and every concurrent search holds a context from the engine's pool, which grows to
the highest concurrency ever reached and does not shrink.

The same split governs the work that runs inside this process rather than in a job. Indexing
and calibration divide their work into batches, one task each, and the engine takes the batch
count from the number of threads; this server caps it at the share reserved for batch work,
so that an append that triggers `index!` does not spread over the threads answering queries.
A job needs no such cap: it is a subprocess started with its share in `JULIA_NUM_THREADS`.
`serve` prints both numbers when it starts. The first specification of the server
(`CHANGELOG.md` §2) proposed a request collector for this: a channel and a pool of worker
tasks that every search would pass through. This is the bound without that structure, and
the measurements a collector would be justified by are the ones above.

`[resources]` divides this server's threads between answering queries and executing jobs. A
job runs as its own process, so the reserved share is spent as a number of processes and a
number of threads each: at most four jobs at once, each with its part of
`floor(threads × batch_threads_pct / 100)`, and never more than that share in total. The
remaining threads stay with the server. `serve` prints the resulting numbers when it starts,
for example `at most 4 concurrent job(s), 3 thread(s) each (20.0% of this server's 64
thread(s))`.

The number of threads the server itself has is the one given to Julia when it starts
(`julia -t auto`), not a value in this file.

## 7. Tests

The suite has two levels. A run can also select some of its files.

- **light** (364 assertions, approximately 36 s, measured on 2026-11-25): the interface with
  the engine. It verifies the mapping from the names used in requests to engine types, from
  engine errors to status codes and exit codes, and from the items of a request to engine
  items. It also verifies that the Julia client has every error type of the engine. No server
  is started and no subprocess is created. This level detects a change in the engine on the
  day it is made.
- **full** (1,450 assertions, approximately 13 minutes with 8 threads, measured on 2026-11-24):
  the end-to-end suites for the API, the jobs, the command lines and the clients. They start a
  server and execute subprocesses. The tests of the command lines run most commands in the test
  process.

```bash
julia --project=server -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.develop(path="."); Pkg.test()'
julia --project=server -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.test(test_args=["full"])'
```

Each test file has a name and a list of tags. The table `TEST_FILES` in
`server/test/runtests.jl` lists them. The names are `config`, `boundary`, `dispatcher`, `e2e`, `api/01` to
`api/21` and `cli/01` to `cli/08`. Examples of tags are `jobs`, `responses`, `client`,
`partitions`, `followers`, `plugins`, `storage`, `auth` and `cli`. A run that receives names or tags includes only the files that
match one of them. The word `light` adds the files of the light level.

```bash
julia --project=server -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.test(test_args=["jobs", "client"])'
julia --project=server -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.test(test_args=["light", "api/17"])'
SSE_TEST_SELECT="api/13 api/17" julia --project=server -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.test()'
```

A name or tag that matches no file stops the run with an error, which lists the valid names and
tags. Each file creates its own datasets, so a file can run without the files before it. The
engine's suite uses the same selection: its files are `dense`, `text`, `persistence`,
`text_partitions` and others, listed in `test/runtests.jl`.

  a token.
